goal: The product-words sweep (embeddings) asks first, with one index probe on product_translations.text_changed_at (step 0.28's mark), whether any product text changed since its previous run began or that run left work behind; when not, and outside the daily full check at 03 UTC, an idle tick reads no product, translation, variant or AI provider.
why: The hourly embeddings sweep reads every active store's products, translations and terms to compare hashes even when no text changed, which is most of the reads of commerce.product_variants and products on an idle day. After the step an idle run is one statement, a changed text or a backlog is embedded on the next run, and a change to a product's categories or tags is caught by the daily full check.

commits.title: The product-words sweep reads no product when no text changed

changes.how: Step 0.28 put the text marker on product_translations.text_changed_at (it refused a column on commerce.products: an update of products runs its publishing check and queues a product.updated event). Confirm with rg -n 'textChangedAt' src/db/schema.ts (it sits in productTranslations); if it is missing, stop (step 0.28 not done). In refreshEmbeddings() (line 110), before `aiFor(null, ...)`, add one statement: `select exists (select 1 from commerce.product_translations t where t.text_changed_at > coalesce((select j.last_started_at from commerce.cron_jobs j where j.job = 'dispatcher.embeddings'), '-infinity'::timestamptz)) or coalesce((select j.last_worked_at >= j.last_started_at from commerce.cron_jobs j where j.job = 'dispatcher.embeddings'), false) as changed` (read through typedRow with { changed: col.bool }). The ledger row is written when a run finishes, so while this run reads it, it holds the previous run: last_started_at is when that run began (a text changed while it ran is newer, so it is not missed), and last_worked_at >= last_started_at (step 3.3's column, set when workedOf() found embedded or failed above 0) says the previous run embedded or failed something, so it may have left more than PER_RUN (256) translations behind or a failure to retry: the sweep goes on until a run finds nothing; when false and the UTC hour is not 3, return { embedded: 0, failed: 0 } without reading a product, a translation or an AI provider. A new translation gets now() from the column's default, so it counts as changed. A category or tag added to or removed from a product (commerce.product_terms, the third input of the hash at lines 31 to 45) moves no marker: the full hash check at UTC hour 3 is the daily net that embeds those, so such a change waits at most a day; say so in the function's comment. Also replace `commerce.store_is_active(t.store_id)` in staleTranslations() (line 41) by `join commerce.stores s on s.id = t.store_id` and, in the where, `s.status = 'active' and not s.starter and not s.sandbox`: the function's whole body is `SELECT COALESCE((SELECT s.status = 'active' AND NOT s.starter AND NOT s.sandbox FROM commerce.stores s WHERE s.id = p_store), false)` (baseline_1_schema.sql line 18852), and a join gives the same rows because a translation's store always exists. If step 3.3 removed a minute guard from this function, leave it removed.

In productTranslations (rg -n 'export const productTranslations' src/db/schema.ts), in its third argument add `index("product_translations_text_changed_idx").on(t.textChangedAt)` so the exists() above is one index probe. Run pnpm db:generate: it writes one plain `CREATE INDEX` on commerce.product_translations, which is not a hot table (the list in CLAUDE.md), so no concurrently and no no-transaction file. If step 0.28 already made such an index, add nothing. Add no column to commerce.products and no trigger.

Existing cases must pass (a changed product gets a new vector through the save path). Add: an idle refreshEmbeddings() reads 0 rows from commerce.products, commerce.product_translations and commerce.product_variants (pg_stat_user_tables difference after pg_stat_force_next_flush()); after a translation's title changes, the next run embeds that product. Make the run before the idle one go through tracked('dispatcher.embeddings', 3600, () => refreshEmbeddings()) from './cron-runs' so its ledger row exists, as production's would. Add: a run right after one that worked (a cron_jobs row with last_worked_at >= last_started_at) reads the translations although no text is newer.

Step 1.10 made this test; step 3.3 made Part A call `entry.run(() => {})` for each key of DISPATCHER_JOBS, once unmeasured (the warm-up) and once inside measure(). Part A does not go through runRegistry, so no ledger row is written, and refreshEmbeddings() now reads its own row in commerce.cron_jobs. For the key embeddings only, run the warm-up through `tracked("dispatcher.embeddings", 3600, () => entry.run(() => {}))` (import tracked from './cron-runs'), so the measured run sees the warm-up as the previous run, as in production. Leave every other key as it is.

Step 1.10 keeps the idle tick's figures under the key queryBudget here, and its test fails when a figure FELL until the baseline is lowered. After the code above, on a freshly seeded database (node scripts/db-setup.mjs --seed), run `UPDATE_BASELINE=1 pnpm vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mts src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts` (it only lowers). In the diff of this file only the figures of dispatcher.embeddings may change, and only downwards; if the test refuses because a figure would rise, stop. Never type a figure by hand.

checked_in_code: Split (12 November) out of step 3.6's commit 5. I opened embeddings.ts: refreshEmbeddings() (line 110) calls aiFor(null) and staleTranslations() (line 41), which reads every active store's translations with products and terms on each run; commerce.store_is_active()'s body is quoted from baseline_1_schema.sql line 18852. Second check (12 November): it reads step 0.28's product_translations.text_changed_at with a plain index on that table, with product_terms changes left to the daily full check. Found while splitting: the old first read compared with cron_jobs.last_ok_at, which record() writes at the run's finish, so a text changed while a run was going would be skipped until 03 UTC, and a run that left more than PER_RUN (256) translations or failed at the provider (refreshEmbeddings() returns failed instead of throwing, so last_ok_at still moves) would stop the sweep until 03 UTC; it now compares with the previous run's last_started_at and goes on while the previous run worked (step 3.3's last_worked_at). Step 1.10's query budget runs jobs outside runRegistry, so no ledger row would exist and the idle skip could not show there; the embeddings warm-up now goes through tracked().
